claims.text: Increasing the solidification cooling rate will refine the eutectic microstructure of a high-entropy alloy.
Cooling-rate-induced eutectic refinement will simultaneously increase strength and ductility.
Conventional cooling rates produce relatively coarse lamellar spacing in the target eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Rapid solidification processing can be used to apply a higher cooling rate during alloy synthesis.
A higher cooling rate will produce a finer lamellar microstructure with reduced spacing between the soft and hard eutectic phases.
Finer lamellar spacing increases the density of interfaces.
The increased interface density creates more barriers to dislocation motion.
Increased resistance to dislocation motion enhances alloy strength.
A well-distributed dual-phase structure improves load sharing.
Improved load sharing delays strain localization and thereby improves ductility.
Rapidly solidified samples are expected to exhibit approximately 15–20% higher yield strength than conventionally processed samples.
Rapidly solidified samples are expected to exhibit approximately 15–20% higher plastic ductility than conventionally processed samples.
The beneficial effects should hold only when cooling-rate optimization avoids detrimental non-equilibrium phases.
The beneficial effects should hold only when cooling-rate optimization avoids excessive residual stresses.
The magnitude of improvement and optimum cooling rate may depend on alloy composition and processing conditions.
